叙.meaning: A king has <part>too much</part> gold in his vaults, so he melts some into shiny medals shaped like a <part>pretzel</part>. He hangs one round the neck of every baker, poet and dog in town. It takes all week. Never has a king had so many honours to <kanji>confer</kanji>.
叙.on: The last medal goes to a <sound>jo</sound>gger who runs in late, still puffing.
叙.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the king, and the dog squeaks '<sound>Ee</sound>!' as the medal tickles its nose.

湖.meaning: Every night a tired, <part>old</part> <part>moon</part> sinks down from the sky to soak its aching craters. Its <part>water drops</part> splash over the hills and gather in a valley, cool and still. By morning the moon is gone, but its bath stays behind as a <kanji>lake</kanji>.
湖.on: A sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala paddles out on a log to look for moon dust.
湖.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat floats a yu<sound>zu</sound> and a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don across it to another <sound>mee</sound>rkat on the far shore.

擁.meaning: A sailor drops his <part>anchor</part> in the harbour, and a soaked <part>sparrow</part> flutters onto the cooking pot's <part>lid</part>, shivering. He tucks it into his beard, adds a <part>scribble</part> to the logbook, 'one new crew', and squeezes it gently. Every bird deserves a <kanji>hug</kanji>.
擁.on: To cheer it up he spins a <sound>yo</sound>-yo, and the sparrow rides the string round and round.

丘.meaning: A woodcutter swears to stop chopping trees, so he buries his <part>axe</part> under <part>one</part> long heap of earth. Grass grows over it, sheep lie on it, kids roll down it. Only the handle pokes out of the top like a flagpole. His promise became a gentle <kanji>hill</kanji>.
丘.on: Kids slide down it on a tea tray, steering with a pool <sound>cue</sound>.
丘.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps a sheep, as a kite shaped like a <sound>ca</sound>rp snags on the axe handle.

咲.meaning: An <part>alien</part> lands in a grey car park and opens its wide <part>mouth</part> to say hello. Instead of words, out pour petals: pink, white and gold. They take root in the cracks, and by the time it flies off the whole car park has begun to <kanji>blossom</kanji>.
咲.on: People drive for miles to see the car park's flower <sound>show</sound>.
咲.kun: A cat stretches out among the flowers, nibbling a <sound>sa</sound>rdine.

鎮.meaning: A dragon storms through the market, roaring. A tiny hypnotist steps up, swings a <part>gold</part> coin on a string and whispers, 'It's <part>true</part>, you're very sleepy.' The dragon's eyes droop and it curls up by the fish stall. One coin was enough to <kanji>tranquilize</kanji> it.
鎮.on: It snores with its huge <sound>chin</sound> resting on the coin.
鎮.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p tucks a blanket over it, and the hypnotist sets a yu<sound>zu</sound> by its nose to smell.

魂.meaning: Every night a <part>ghost</part> sits on the church roof flying a <part>kite</part>. Tied to its tail is something faint and glowing that hums. It isn't the ghost's body; that's long gone. It's the part of him that still loves kites: his <kanji>soul</kanji>.
魂.on: A <sound>con</sound>dor circles the kite, curious about the hum.
魂.kun: He shares a <sound>ta</sound>co with a lla<sound>ma</sound>, a <sound>shee</sound>p and an <sound>ee</sound>l, who all haunt the roof with him.

嬢.meaning: A <part>woman</part> who runs a laundry hears giggling from the <part>laundry pile</part>. Out pops her niece, socks on both hands as gloves, 'helping' by tossing shirts at the ceiling. She folds one towel into a crown, puts it on and bows. Every customer asks after the cheeky little <kanji>lass</kanji>.
嬢.on: She folds a tiny pouch for a <sound>jo</sound>ey that hopped in with the towels.
嬢.kun: '<sound>Mu</sound>!' says a cow at the window; the lass hangs a <sound>su</sound>it to dry on its horns and gives it some <sound>me</sound>lon.

旋.meaning: A bored giant at the swimming pool kicks the <part>diving board</part> with his <part>giant boot</part>. The board spins like a propeller, and a <part>sail</part> someone left on it catches the wind and keeps it whirling all summer. The kids ride it round and round. The pool's best ride is pure <kanji>rotation</kanji>.
旋.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try stands guard so nobody climbs on while it's spinning.
旋.kun: A <sound>me</sound>lon rolls off the end, and a <sound>goo</sound>se chases it round and round the pool.

較.meaning: At a crossroads, a shiny new <part>car</part> and a rusty old banger pull up side by side, and their drivers <part>mingle</part>, chatting window to window. Everyone on the pavement looks from one to the other: gleaming paint, dangling bumper. The two cars are a perfect <kanji>contrast</kanji>.
較.on: On the old car's roof sits a vulture, picking at a chicken <sound>car</sound>cass.
較.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo on a lamppost looks them both over, then shouts '<sound>Rah</sound>!' for the rusty one.
